source.format: Git bundle containing all refs and commit history
source.export_procedure: After committing product source, create a Git bundle with all refs and record the exact exported commit SHA.
source.import_procedure: Clone the bundle into a new working directory, run git fsck --full, and check out the recorded commit.

runtime.interface: Node.js process contract driven by the product manifest; no vendor-specific runtime API.
runtime.version_policy: Pin a supported Node.js LTS major per release and declare product dependencies explicitly.
target_matrix: Linux amd64 (the current CI target only; other targets remain unverified)
runtime.build_definition: examples/hello-world/product.json and the checked-in .mjs product scripts.

dependencies.name: Node.js runtime
dependencies.adapter: Standard node executable invoked through the factory process contract.
dependencies.replacement_plan: Use another conforming Node.js LTS distribution; no cloud account or proprietary runtime service is required.

data_assets.name: source-and-build-definition
data_assets.format: Git bundle plus checked-in JSON and JavaScript source
data_assets.export_procedure: Export all Git refs with git bundle and retain the commit SHA and manifest files.
data_assets.import_procedure: Clone the Git bundle, verify the commit SHA, and install only dependencies declared by the product.
data_assets.integrity_method: git fsck --full, commit SHA comparison, and SHA-256 for exported manifest files.

data_assets.name: factory-ledger-records
data_assets.format: PostgreSQL custom-format dump plus versioned SQL migrations
data_assets.export_procedure: Quiesce workers, create a project-scoped logical export using a privileged migration operator, and retain the schema/migration versions.
data_assets.import_procedure: Restore into an isolated PostgreSQL target, bootstrap roles separately, re-enroll product identities, and run ledger/RLS invariants.
data_assets.integrity_method: Compare stable project/task/attempt identifiers, row counts, foreign keys, event ordering, and SQL invariant tests.

data_assets.name: artifact-payloads-and-evidence
data_assets.format: S3-compatible object payloads plus a JSON manifest containing object keys, sizes, content types, and SHA-256 hashes
data_assets.export_procedure: Enumerate only the product-scoped object prefix and export each payload with its metadata manifest.
data_assets.import_procedure: Copy payloads into a compatible target bucket and restore references only after integrity verification.
data_assets.integrity_method: Recompute SHA-256 and byte size for every payload and compare them with the exported manifest.

artifacts.interface: S3-compatible object API with product-scoped keys; provider-specific SDKs remain replaceable adapters.
artifacts.export_procedure: Export object payloads and a versioned JSON manifest independently of the storage provider.
artifacts.import_procedure: Import through an S3-compatible API and verify all payload hashes before reconnecting ledger references.
artifacts.integrity_method: SHA-256 and byte-size verification for every object.

secrets.rebind_procedure: Create new product-scoped credentials in the target secret manager, re-enroll database identities, and inject secrets only at runtime. Never copy secret values into the export.

backup_restore.backup_format: PostgreSQL custom-format logical dump, Git bundle, and S3-compatible artifact archive with a JSON SHA-256 manifest.
backup_restore.restore_procedure: Restore into a second isolated host, bootstrap roles and secrets independently, import the Git bundle and artifact archive, then run database, authorization, artifact-integrity, and product smoke tests.

exit_cost.notes: Not measured. Estimate only after a complete restore has been rehearsed on a second isolated host, including data transfer, operator time, and service interruption.
